svg.title: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to fix: Every check stops and names the fix, and init finishes cleanly once GitLab is turned off
svg.text: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to
Scenario: Every check stops and names the fix, and init finishes cleanly once GitLab is turned off
The check names each missing tool
The check reads the right GitLab host
init names the exact fix, then bows out cleanly

g.text: Given a developer's project points at the company's own GitLab, with
none of the toolbox's tools installed yet
A copy of the toolbox on a fresh machine. Its git remote points at the company's own GitLab,
gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example.
The toolbox needs three tools: gum, glow and glab, the GitLab command line tool. None of them
is installed yet, and the shell answers "command not found" for each.
When the developer runs the GitLab check and installs only the tool it names, one at a time
The developer runs the GitLab check three times and installs only the tool it names in between. The first run stops at
"Required UI dependency missing: gum", the second at glow.
With both installed, the third run stops in a box, "GitLab CLI not found", and says to install glab. Each run ends on
"Failed to run task". Tool versions show as X.Y.Z.
When the developer installs the GitLab CLI, the check names the
company's GitLab host and offers to sign in
The developer installs glab with task glab:install and runs the check again. Nobody has
signed in yet, so the check shows "GitLab Authentication Required".
"Target Host: gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example" is the host it read from the git remote. Below
it, the check asks "Continue and sign in now?", and waits for Yes or No.
Then an SSH-style gitlabssh remote still leads the check to the same GitLab host
The developer answered No, and now points the remote at the address the company's GitLab gives for SSH clones. git
remote -v shows git@gitlabssh.selfhosted-corp.example.
The check still says "Target Host: gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example". It turns the gitlabssh name back into the gitlab
one, the address where you sign in.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin git@gitlabssh.selfhosted-corp.example:acme/widgets.git && git remote -v && task

g.text: Then a GitHub remote is refused, with the exact command to point it back at GitLab
Now the remote points at github.com. The check stops at once with "No GitLab repository remote was detected." It never
asks to sign in.
It prints the exact line that points the remote back at GitLab, git remote set-url origin
https://gitlab.com/<namespace>/<project>.git, and then task devsecops:init.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/acme/widgets.git && git remote -v && task glab:auth:ensure

g.text: When the developer points the remote back at GitLab and runs init, it stops at the sign-in
and names the command to run
The developer follows that advice with gitlab.com and runs init. It first installs every tool the project needs, a long
run that scrolls off the screen, so the card starts at its last line, "Development environment setup completed
successfully".
Then init reaches its GitLab step and shows the same sign-in card, now for "Target Host: gitlab.com". The developer
answers No, and init pauses with the two commands to run, "task glab:auth" and then "task devsecops:init".

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://gitlab.com/acme/widgets.git && task devsecops:init

g.text: Then a project that stays on GitHub turns the GitLab integration off,
and init finishes cleanly
A project that stays on GitHub has no GitLab to sign in to. It turns the GitLab part of the
toolbox off with TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false and runs init on its GitHub remote.
The card starts on the same line as the card before. This time init skips its GitLab step
(the task runner says devsecops:init:configure "is up to date") and goes straight to
"DevSecOps project initialization completed". No sign-in question, no refusal of the remote.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/acme/widgets.git && TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false
